subject: Optima Health - Private VPC: transient control-plane heartbeat degradation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julian Martinez <julian.martinez@optima-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Optima Health - Private VPC: transient control-plane heartbeat degradation

Julian —

I wanted to notify you directly: between ~08:45–09:05 PDT we observed a spike of transient heartbeat drops between the Optima private VPC agents and Redwood’s control plane. Impact: short reconnects for a subset of inference requests (p95 latency increased briefly, some requests retried automatically).

What we know so far:
- Root cause appears to be an edge autoscaling race on our control plane path — a subset of control-plane connections saw TCP retransmits during a single scaling event.
- Approx ~3% of requests to your private deployment experienced a retry; no model state loss observed.
- Our runtime automatically failed over to warm connection pools; no customer data was exposed.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled a targeted rollback of the recent control-plane scaling change at 08:58 PDT.
- Enabled conservative connection backoff for Optima’s tenant while we validate traces.
- Captured heartbeat traces and socket metrics — attached for your ops team.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) Short customer bridge right now (15–20m) to walk through what we captured.
2) Postmortem with a remediation plan and timeline tomorrow, plus a proposed maintenance window for a permanent fix.

I can hop on a call in 15 minutes if that works for you — otherwise I’ll schedule a 30 minute bridge at 10:00 PDT.

Sorry for the interruption; we’ll keep this tightly scoped and transparent.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:36:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Optima Health - Private VPC: transient control-plane heartbeat degradation

Ben / Marissa —

Summary of the signal we pulled from the traces (more detail in the attached zip):
- At ~08:47:30 we saw a cluster-level control-plane autoscaler perform a scale-out that briefly exhausted ephemeral connection slots on the control-plane egress path.
- This caused a burst of SYN/ACK retransmits and ~15–25s TCP connect stalls for a subset of agents in Optima’s VPC zone.
- Our warm-connection fallback kicked in and requests were transparently retried at the SDK layer — that’s why most end-user requests succeeded after a slight delay.

Mitigations applied (live):
- Reverted the autoscaler patch (08:58).
- Tightened ephemeral slot allocation for tenant-scoped pools.
- Increased socket backlog and introduced a conservative connect jitter for Optima tenant.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Q1: Hard cap for concurrent connect spikes + pre-warming for known tenant bursts.
- Q2: Improved autoscaler probe and graceful drain to avoid transient slot exhaustion.

Risk to your nightly jobs: none expected — the rollback returned things to baseline and we’ve scheduled additional soak monitoring. If you prefer, we can block a low-risk maintenance window this week and fully validate in your staging cluster first.

I’ll join the 10:00 bridge to walk through traces with your ops team.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao | Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Optima Health - Private VPC: transient control-plane heartbeat degradation

Julian —

Thanks for confirming. Quick summary from this morning’s bridge and next actions (so we keep a single source of truth):
- Root cause: control-plane autoscaler scale-out transiently exhausting ephemeral connection slots (confirmed by the traces).
- Immediate customer-facing mitigations: rollback applied, tenant-level connection jitter + backlog increased.
- Short-term plan (this week): extended monitoring (72h) and low-risk maintenance window to run a staged pre-warm in your staging VPC (we propose Thu 2027-09-02 02:00–04:00 PDT).
- Long-term: autoscaler probe improvements + pre-warming runway (Q4 engineering deliverable).

Requested from Optima:
1) Approve the proposed maintenance window for the staging pre-warm.
2) Share any blackout windows for your teams (nightly ETL at 02:00 was noted — we can shift the pre-warm).
3) Confirmation if you want a formal credit for the retry-induced cost delta (we’ll compute and propose).

We’ll follow up with a short postmortem doc by tomorrow EOD (attached once ready).

Thanks,
Ben
